subject: History
topic: Independence Movement — key leaders, events, civil disobedience

questions.stem: Who led the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930?
questions.explanation: Civil Disobedience Movement (1930): led by Gandhi. Salt March from Sabarmati to Dandi. Mass civil disobedience against British salt monopoly. Answer: B. Trap: A/C/D (participated but didn't lead overall movement).

questions.stem: In which year did India become independent?
questions.explanation: India became independent on August 15, 1947. Republic Day (Constitution adopted) = January 26, 1950. Answer: C. Trap: A (WWII end), B (interim), D (Constitution/Republic).

questions.stem: What was the Quit India Movement?

options.option_text: Demand for immediate British withdrawal from India (1942)

questions.explanation: Quit India Movement (August 1942): led by Gandhi. Resolution demanding immediate British withdrawal. Mass civil disobedience. Answer: A. Trap: B (Cabinet Mission Plan), C (Partition), D (post-1947).

questions.stem: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru: first PM (1947-1964). Architect of modern India. Answer: B. Trap: A (freedom fighter, not PM), C (Deputy PM), D (Education Minister).

questions.stem: The Partition of India (1947) resulted in the creation of which countries?
questions.explanation: 1947 Partition: India and Pakistan (East & West). East Pakistan became Bangladesh in 1971. Answer: A (immediate result of 1947 partition). Trap: B (Bangladesh formed later), C (Nepal unrelated), D (Pakistan as one country initially, though geographically divided).

questions.stem: Which movement was associated with 'Jai Hind' and Indian National Army (INA)?

options.option_text: Subhas Chandra Bose's INA and Azad Hind movement

questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose led Indian National Army (INA). 'Jai Hind' popularized by INA. Armed struggle for independence during WWII. Answer: B. Trap: A (religious reform), C (boycott of foreign goods), D (intellectual movement).

questions.stem: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's primary contribution to independent India was:

options.option_text: Chairing the Drafting Committee of the Constitution
Leading the Civil Disobedience Movement (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: B.R. Ambedkar: Chairman of Constituent Assembly's Drafting Committee. Architect of Indian Constitution. Champion of equality and rights for marginalized. Answer: B. Trap: A (Bose), C (Gandhi), D (Gandhi).
